newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call money stuck at highs.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call money stuck at highs.

text.p: Dutch call money rates were stuck at an extremely high level for the second day in a row on Friday with liquidity unevenly divided ahead of the expiry of the three-month secured loans pact.
Call money was trading at 3.12 percent bid, but one dealer said some trades were done at 3.25 percent.

"It is (going for) whatever a fool is willing to pay," the dealer said, adding overnight money rates would return to normal levels at the start of next week when the Dutch central bank sets a new special advances pact. This will be followed by a new three-monthly credit quota on Friday.
Every three months the central sets a quota on the amount banks can borrow through its regular credit facilities at the secured loans rate, currently 2.00 percent.
"Some participants might have eaten up their quota," said one dealer, adding they had to search for overnight money in the money market.
"The tight allocation under the current advances pact does not offer much solace," said one dealer.
This week the central bank allocated 2.11 billion guilders under a seven-day pact and individual banks' applications were met up to 2.50 billion guilders for just over 10 percent.
Dealers said they foresee the call money rate going down to around 2.62 percent bid early next week.
The guilder was a little stronger against the mark at 112.15 per 100 marks versus 112.18 on Thursday.
